cards.text: Once again Jesus goes out beside the sea. ALL the people come to Him, and He teaches them right there. Friend, ALL the people. I couldn't get all six of my kids to the counter at the same time.
As Jesus walks along, He sees Levi son of Alphaeus, a tax collector, sitting at the tax booth. That's the one window in town where NOBODY walks up smiling.

cards.question: Jesus stops at the tax booth and speaks to Levi son of Alphaeus. What does He tell him?
Jesus tells Levi to follow Him. Levi asks for some time to think it over first.

cards.text: Levi gets up and follows Him. Friend, it took me YEARS to get out of a junk drawer, and this man gets up out of his booth just like that.
Next thing you know, Jesus is dining at Levi's house with His disciples. And it's a FULL house, because there were many who followed Him.

cards.question: At Levi's house, many tax collectors and ___ are eating with Jesus and His disciples.

cards.text: A dinner like this gets noticed. Somebody's watching, and I bet they've got their arms crossed so tight they can't reach the cookie box.

cards.question: Who sees Jesus eating with tax collectors and sinners at Levi's house?
The scribes who were Pharisees want to know why Jesus eats with tax collectors and sinners. They take that question straight to Jesus.

cards.text: They ask His disciples instead, and Jesus hears it. That's like whispering 'Why does the boss DO that?' to your coworker while the boss is standing right behind you.

cards.question: Jesus answers the scribes with a picture from everyday life. Who does He say needs a doctor?
Then Jesus tells the scribes, 'I have not come to call the ___, but ___.'

cards.text: Now, John the Baptist's disciples and the Pharisees are often fasting. So people come to Jesus with a question, and I bet somebody's been keeping score.

cards.question: People come to Jesus about fasting. They ask why His disciples don't fast like the disciples of John and of the Pharisees.

cards.text: Jesus answers with a picture everybody knows: a wedding. There's the bridegroom, and there are the bridegroom's guests.

cards.question: In Jesus' wedding picture, when does He say the bridegroom's guests cannot fast?

cards.text: But Jesus doesn't stop there. He says the time will come when things change for those guests.

cards.question: What does Jesus say will happen to the bridegroom when that time comes?

answers.text: He will be taken from them
He will start a new feast

cards.question: Jesus says that once the bridegroom is taken from them, the guests will fast.

cards.text: Then Jesus gives two more everyday pictures. First up: an old garment and a patch of unshrunk cloth, and friend, I know OLD, I spent years in a junk drawer collecting dust like it was my job.

cards.question: What does Jesus say happens if someone sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment?

answers.text: The new piece pulls away and the tear gets worse
The patch shrinks down to a perfect fit
The old cloth turns as strong as new

cards.question: Jesus says people often sew patches of unshrunk cloth onto old garments.

cards.text: Second picture: new wine and old wineskins. Same idea, different container, and you can already hear the trouble coming.

cards.question: What does Jesus say happens if someone pours new wine into old wineskins?

answers.text: The skins make the wine better

cards.question: Jesus says that when new wine goes into old wineskins, both the ___ and the ___ will be ruined.
So instead, what does Jesus say is done with new wine?

answers.text: New wine goes into new wineskins
Old wine goes into new wineskins
New wine goes into old jars

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Once again…', 'ALL the people come…', 'Friend, ALL the people.' and 'I couldn't get all six…'. That is over the 3-sentence limit.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to the backstory that clashes with it. Every cutter was 'set down right next to Dorin' on the counter, so he never had to get his kids to the counter. The joke is also set in the Millers' kitchen, not his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: 'Next thing you know' says the dinner comes right after Levi's call. Mark 2:15 only says 'While Jesus was dining at Levi's house' and gives no time link to the call.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: 'Jesus answers the scribes' says who Jesus is speaking to. Mark 2:17 only says 'Jesus told them', and 'them' could be the scribes or the disciples. The text leaves this open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Then Jesus tells the scribes' says who Jesus is speaking to, but Mark 2:17 only says 'Jesus told them'.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'I bet somebody's been keeping score' gives the people a reason for their question: comparing and keeping a tally. Mark 2:18 gives only the setup ('So people came…'), not this reason. The 'I bet' rule is for feelings, not reasons.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The joke only shares the word 'old' with the fact. The core action of the picture is a new patch pulling away from an old garment and making a worse tear. Papa Dorin collecting dust in the drawer doesn't have that action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'You can already hear the trouble coming' tells the baker the outcome is bad before card 5. That rules out the wrong answer 'The skins make the wine better', and 'hear' hints at bursting.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Same idea, different container' calls the garment a container, which isn't true. It also says how the two pictures connect, which the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The question asks what is done 'with new wine', so the wrong answer 'Old wine goes into new wineskins' doesn't answer the question and is ruled out by its wording. It isn't the same kind of thing as the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
